//: Curated benchmark set for the nightly benchlab run. Each target is measured at three commits in one benchlab invocation, so the cost of adding a target is roughly three times its plain benchmark time -- see build/bench-nightly/main.go. Cost is per case and independent of how fast the case is, since -benchtime is fixed: one case is reps * benchtime * 3 arms. The full published set is ~1118 cases, far too many to measure this way nightly. A target without a "bench" selects its package's BenchmarkBenchlab* wrappers, defined in that package's benchlab_test.go, which is where the set is decided.

targets.//: The eval driver, iteration and enumerate, bindings, comprehension indexing, the rule index, and partial eval. The sweeps this replaces re-measured one code path at several sizes, which at a fixed cost per case bought nothing.

Compilation, the rule index, parsing, object/set/array internals, refs and value conversion. Excludes the NoASTTypeAllocates*/NoNodeTypeAllocates* families, which are allocation assertions rather than trend material.

The public evaluation API, the closest thing here to end-to-end user-visible performance. The *Targets families measure their shape once per evaluation target, which is the only place topdown and wasm are tracked against each other.
The store read/write hot path, each family measured against all three store representations -- Go, Go with a round trip on write, and AST -- which is the comparison this package exists to make.
opa build over increasingly many dynamically-selected policies, and against large partial rule sets. Both families exist because of filed regressions (#5216, #5756).
Any.Merge/Union, reached from types.Or on the type checker's hot path, plus Type.Select.
opa fmt / LSP formatting of a large policy.
WASM eval, the Rego-to-WASM compiler, and a Go arm to compare against. Requires the opa_wasm build tag, which is already the default.
The coverage tracer's overhead, paid by every opa test --coverage run.
The profiler's overhead, on the same shapes as v1/cover so the two are comparable.
A comprehension-heavy Kubernetes policy, compiled and evaluated per iteration.
opa deps. The lowest-value target in this shard; cut first if the shard needs to shrink.
Bundle activation and ingest: root-conflict detection per conflict shape, the tarball and directory loaders, signature hashing and the per-activation deep copy.
Decision-log cost per logged decision: event-to-AST conversion, and masking with and without a rule that fires.
The canonical OPA-as-API-authorization policy through a prepared query. The disk arm is excluded; it measures Badger rather than the policy.
The data and compile handlers, in-process rather than over a socket. Note newBenchFixture binds a fixed port, so keep server in one shard.
util.RoundTripFast, on the path of every store write, logged decision and rego result, with the legacy RoundTrip as a comparison anchor.
